Ship a lossless WebP only where every decoder draws it the same as the PNG, and recompress the other masters as PNG with their pixels proved identical (r38-bytes repair; D-351; both games, shared build plumbing)

The independent check of 2026-10-03 failed `safe` on two findings. B1: art/characters/yunalesca-3/idle@2x is cleaned by PaintedMatte.cleanMatte
through a 2D canvas on a desktop, where Chromium's WebP and PNG decoders premultiply differently (24,069 pixels by up to 124 in 255; the game's
cleaned canvas hashed 1470abcc against the PNG build's adee2707), and the identity tool had exempted every 2x master as "texture only". B2: in
Playwright's WebKit a WebP loses the colour under fully transparent pixels where its PNG keeps it. The driver's decision was to ship the
decoder-independent set as the default.

- New default scope `exact` (DEFAULT_SCOPE): a master ships as a lossless WebP only if premultiplying alpha is the identity on every one of its
  pixels, so every decoder draws the WebP and the PNG the same: it is opaque, or its alpha is only 0 and 255 with no colour left under alpha 0
  (decoderIndependent in the new tools/art-image-facts.mjs, read from the decoded master by alphaInfoOf and cached by its hash; an unknown fact is a
  no). 482 of 897 masters (63 opaque, 419 binary alpha). Every other master ships as a PNG, the 24 2x masters included: yunalesca-3/idle@2x is PNG.
- D-351's "tighter PNG compression", which the check found unapplied, now covers every kept PNG: libvips level 9 with adaptive filtering and no
  palette, the metadata chunks libvips adds dropped (stripAncillaryChunks), each proved to decode to the master's RGBA in all four channels (colour
  under alpha 0 included) before it is cached, shipped only when smaller. 283 shrink by 13,956,357 bytes; 132 are not smaller and ship as the
  master's own bytes. Re-deflating the same scanlines with Node's zlib gains only 0.1 to 0.4 percent, so this is where zlib-class compression ends.
- verifyShippedArt, the deploy's gate, is strict by default: a WebP of a master that has partly transparent pixels or colour under alpha 0 is a

Version 1.1.1: build against RuneLite's widened exchange API

RuneLite changed GrandExchangeOffer.getPrice() and getSpent(), and
ItemManager.getItemPrice(), from int to long. A jar compiled against the old
signatures fails to link on a current client, which RuneLite reports as "Plugin
is incompatible, requires update by its author". Version 1.1.0 was built before
the change and is affected; the plugin does not compile against the current
client without this.

The types follow the API: the remembered baseline (SavedOffer price and spent),
the previous-total parameters on the fill path, and the watchlist's price are
long now. Old saved baselines deserialise into the wider field unchanged.

The gross value of a fill is still the difference of the client's running total
taken as 32 bits. RuneLite widening the getter does not say the game's counter
stopped wrapping, and the modulo-2^32 difference is exact whether it did or not:
a single fill is kept under 2^31 by the check before it, so that difference is
the true one either way, and a stale baseline gives a huge value that the
existing checks send to the estimate. Dropping that arithmetic for a plain long
subtraction would have regressed the wrapped-total case, and the existing test
for it caught exactly that.

The test doubles that implement GrandExchangeOffer return long to match. All 398
tests pass against the current RuneLite release.
